claims.claim_text: The indexed Mary D. Bancroft is the Zurich-based writer and translator who worked for Allen Dulles's OSS station.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The distinctive name, Zurich residence, language work, Dulles relationship, and direct OSS documentation align.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence; two institutional archival descriptions document the same Mary Bancroft's Zurich and OSS chronology.
claims.temporal_assessment: Freelance work is dated 1938-1953 and OSS intelligence work 1941-1945.
claims.match_notes: The Box 34 personnel file remains unreviewed; the index contains a middle initial not expanded by the accessible sources.

claims.claim_text: Mary Bancroft's best-supported immediate civilian affiliation was freelance journalism and translation in Zurich.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: Harvard describes her freelance translation and Swiss journalism; Columbia dates that work across her OSS years.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence; the archival descriptions align on name, place, work, dates, and OSS connection.
claims.temporal_assessment: Strongly date-bounded and overlapping OSS service; the freelance work did not necessarily end at recruitment.
claims.match_notes: This is self-employment. Die Weltwoche published some articles, but the sources do not establish a staff employment relationship.

claims.claim_text: Mary Bancroft's last documented civilian working status before OSS was self-employed journalist, writer, and translator.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: Institutional finding aids document freelance writing and translation in Zurich before and during OSS service.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence; two archival institutions describe the same distinctive career and wartime chronology.
claims.temporal_assessment: The work is documented from 1938 and continued during the OSS period.
claims.match_notes: No named employer is inferred from publication of her work.

claims.claim_text: The indexed Stephanie Czech is Stephanie Czech Rader, the WAC captain assigned by OSS to Poland in 1945.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: CIA uses her birth name, documents her captaincy and Polish-language skills, and dates her OSS assignment to fall 1945.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence; the exact distinctive birth name and unusually specific official service chronology align.
claims.temporal_assessment: The official biography sequences civilian work, WAAC/WAC service, and OSS assignment.
claims.match_notes: The Box 162 file remains unreviewed; the private index serial number is not reproduced.

claims.claim_text: Stephanie Czech's immediate pre-OSS affiliation was the Women's Army Corps, where she held the rank of captain.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: CIA places her WAAC/WAC officer service immediately before OSS noticed her skills and assigned her to Poland.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence; exact name, language background, military rank, and official OSS chronology align.
claims.temporal_assessment: Explicit sequence into an OSS assignment in fall 1945.
claims.match_notes: The source says WAAC; Army history documents its 1943 conversion to WAC. This was military assignment, not civilian employment.

claims.claim_text: Stephanie Czech's last civilian employer before WAAC/WAC and OSS service was the Texas Oil Company in New York.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: CIA documents her librarian and researcher job, followed by wartime volunteering and later OSS selection.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence; the exact birth name and detailed education, employment, military, and OSS sequence are official.
claims.temporal_assessment: Strongly date-bounded; WAAC/WAC service intervened before OSS.
claims.match_notes: The employer name is preserved exactly as CIA gives it; no modern successor is substituted.

claims.claim_text: The indexed Elizabeth P. MacDonald is journalist Elizabeth Betty Peet MacDonald, later Elizabeth Peet McIntosh.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: CIA and NPS connect the married indexed name, Peet birth name, later McIntosh name, journalism, and OSS Morale Operations service.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence; exact indexed initials and a specific sequence of names, journalism, language skills, and OSS service align.
claims.temporal_assessment: Pacific journalism preceded OSS recruitment in 1943.
claims.match_notes: The Box 470 personnel file remains unreviewed; no serial number appears in the source row.

claims.claim_text: Elizabeth MacDonald's best-supported immediate pre-OSS affiliation was Pacific reporting for Scripps-Howard News Service.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: CIA documents her Scripps Howard reporting after Pearl Harbor and later OSS recruitment; NPS calls her a former Pacific war correspondent.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence; official sources align on her names, profession, theater expertise, and OSS chronology.
claims.temporal_assessment: Strongly date-bounded between Pearl Harbor and her 1943 OSS entry.
claims.match_notes: No intervening affiliation was found in the official sources reviewed.

claims.claim_text: Elizabeth MacDonald's last documented civilian employer before OSS was Scripps-Howard News Service.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: CIA places Scripps Howard reporting immediately before later OSS recruitment; NPS corroborates her former Pacific correspondent status.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence; official sources supply a specific and internally consistent identity and employment chronology.
claims.temporal_assessment: Strongly date-bounded before OSS entry in 1943.
claims.match_notes: This civilian employer is distinct from her later OSS government assignment.

claims.claim_text: Before her Scripps-Howard work, Elizabeth MacDonald reported sports and feature stories for the Honolulu Advertiser.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: CIA documents the Honolulu Advertiser job before her Pearl Harbor reporting for Scripps Howard.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence; the official biography provides a continuous named career sequence.
claims.temporal_assessment: Documented prewar employment, but not the immediate pre-OSS role.
claims.match_notes: The earlier newspaper is not substituted for the later Scripps-Howard affiliation.

claims.claim_text: The indexed Jane Foster is the Mills College graduate and artist who served as an OSS civilian in Morale Operations.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The official index and a CIA scholarly study align on exact name, civilian status, education, occupation, and Indonesia expertise.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence; the exact name is supported by an unusually specific official personnel and assignment description.
claims.temporal_assessment: The source places prewar Netherlands East Indies residence before her OSS work.
claims.match_notes: The Box 245 file remains unreviewed. Later allegations and postwar activity are outside this profile's research question.

claims.claim_text: Jane Foster's documented occupation at the time of her OSS service was artist.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: William J. Rust's CIA study describes Foster as a 32-year-old artist working in OSS Morale Operations.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence; exact name, age, education, civilian status, branch, and geographic expertise form a specific match.
claims.temporal_assessment: Contemporaneous with OSS service; no named pre-OSS employer is established.
claims.match_notes: Occupation alone is not converted into self-employment or a named employer.

claims.claim_text: Before OSS, Jane Foster attended and graduated from Mills College.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The CIA study identifies Foster as a Mills College graduate.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence; the education detail is part of the same specific official OSS biography.
claims.match_notes: Mills College is not presented as an employer.

claims.claim_text: The indexed Stella T. Uzdawinis is the civilian OSS R&A and Secret Intelligence communicator documented by the CIA Museum.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The exact distinctive name and official artifact description identify her civilian OSS branches and France communicator assignment.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence; an exceptionally distinctive name and direct official institutional record align.
claims.temporal_assessment: The CIA source documents OSS and postwar service but does not state her pre-OSS affiliation.
claims.match_notes: The Box 795 file remains unreviewed. No pre-OSS employer is inferred from language ability or later Army civilian service.

research_attempts.query_text: "Mary D Bancroft" OSS; "Mary Bancroft" Dulles; prewar occupation; NARA index, CIA Reading Room, Harvard HOLLIS, Columbia oral history, newspaper, obituary, directory, and archival review
research_attempts.rejection_reasons: Wikipedia and derivative biographies were discovery-only; a newspaper obituary emphasized personal relationships rather than employment; publication by Die Weltwoche did not prove staff employment.
research_attempts.research_notes: Verified self-employed journalism, writing, and translation in Zurich from 1938 across the OSS period. No newspaper employer was inferred.
research_attempts.next_action: Review Box 34 and Mary Bancroft's archival collections for exact recruitment and freelance-work terms.
